title: Streamline API bridge: align cache semantics and remove redundant fanout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Consolidate and simplify the Console API bridge layer that fans out requests to multiple downstream aggregators. Today multiple paths implement slightly different cache keys, TTLs, and invalidation rules which causes stale or duplicated data and contributes to request amplification under contention. This ticket will harmonize cache semantics,: - collapse redundant fanout for the /metrics and /routes endpoints into a single multiplexer, - implement a canonical cache key generator shared by REST and GraphQL resolvers, - reconcile LRU vs TTL trade-offs and expose a single tunable policy in config. Success criteria: 20-40% reduction in p99 tail latency for aggregated requests, 25% fewer downstream calls under median load, and no functional regressions in pagination or freshness checks.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Maya Chen: Initial discovery. Reproduced amplification under synthetic load. Noticed two different cache key constructors in aggregator and graphql resolver. Hypothesis: key drift causes cache misses and duplicate fanout.

2026-02-18 - Arjun Patel: Spike completed. Created a PoC multiplexer that coalesces fanout; observed 30% reduction in downstream calls in local sim. PoC branch: github.com/redwood-inference/console/compare/poC/coalesce-bridge

2026-02-25 - Design review (informal): UX noted that pagination semantics must be preserved for cursor-based endpoints. We will keep per-client cursor headers unchanged and translate in the multiplexer to avoid breaking clients.

2026-03-01 - PR opened: #4821 contains initial refactor extracting canonical cache-key util and a thin multiplexer. Requesting review from @sara, @lee. Note: tests currently mock the old aggregator; integration tests to follow.

2026-03-05 - Performance run: staging benchmark against 10k RPS synthetic traffic. Observed 18% median latency improvement, p99 improved ~22% for aggregated endpoints. Memory use for bridge process increased ~6% due to short-lived coalescing state. Will add LRU eviction tuning.

2026-03-09 - Feedback from infra: coalescer uses a global timer that could interfere with node shutdown. Plan: replace with a request-scoped promise pattern and a shared in-memory sharded map with bounded size.

2026-03-11 - Arjun Patel: Work in progress to add integration tests and update monitoring spans. Marking as In Progress and moving estimate to 5 points. Next: address shutdown race, add end-to-end freshness test against real data set, and schedule runtime canary in us-west-2.
notes: Trade-offs: tight coalescing windows reduce downstream calls but increase memory/latency sensitivity; we will expose coalescing window and LRU size as config flags behind a feature toggle to allow gradual rollout. Consideration given to switching to distributed cache but decided to keep in-process LRU for lower latency and simpler invalidation during this sprint.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for canonical key generator across permutations. 2) Integration test that asserts no duplicate downstream calls for simultaneous requests with same key. 3) Staging canary with 5% traffic for 48 hours and monitoring of error rates, p99 latency, and downstream call count. 4) Rollback plan: toggle feature off to restore previous behavior.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle cache semantics regressions could break freshness-sensitive dashboards. Mitigation: add evaluation suite that compares responses from old vs new bridge across 50 representative queries; run before promoting canary. Risk: increased memory usage during peak; mitigation: configure LRU hard cap and circuit-breaker to bypass coalescer under high memory pressure.
expected_steps: 1. Extract canonical cache-key util and add unit tests. 2. Implement multiplexer and coalescing logic behind toggle. 3. Reconcile TTL/LRU policy and add config knobs. 4. Integration tests and end-to-end comparison harness. 5. Staging canary and rollout. 6. Postmortem and docs update.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All unit and integration tests pass. 2) Staging canary shows <=1% error delta and >=15% reduction in downstream calls for aggregated endpoints. 3) No customer-facing regressions reported in 72h after rollout. 4) Monitoring dashboards updated with new bridge metrics (coalesce_hits, coalesce_misses, bridge_memory_bytes).
